title: High Density Cultivation of Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 using the HDC 6.10B system
author: Oliver Mantovani
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9cgh2tw

steps.title: Prepare 6‑well plate precultures
steps.instruction: Inoculate standard polystyrene 6‑well plates (3 wells per strain, enough for 3 replicates) with 3 mL of BG11 medium per well (or modified BG11 if Cu²⁺/Co²⁺ induction is required). Add the appropriate antibiotics. Place the plates on a standard orbital shaker (Model 5000, VWR; orbit 25 mm; 120 rpm) and incubate at 30 °C under constant light of 50–100 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹ for about 4 days.

steps.title: Inoculate CellDeg cultures
steps.instruction: Measure the OD₇₅₀ of each preculture, calculate the volume needed to obtain an OD₇₅₀ of 0.3 in an 8 mL CellDeg culture (e.g., V_preculture = (0.3 × 8 mL)/1.2 = 2 mL). Centrifuge the calculated volume for 5 min at 2500 g at room temperature, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 8 mL CellDeg medium (including the required antibiotics). If induction is needed, add CuSO₄ to a final concentration of 4 µM every second day (for P_petE) and/or CoCl₂ to 30 µM daily (for P_coaT). Transfer the suspension to a CellDeg vessel; optionally add 2 mL dodecane on top for in‑situ extraction (resulting in a total volume of 10 mL). If no dodecane is used, keep the culture volume at 10 mL.

steps.title: Prepare bicarbonate‑carbonate buffer
steps.instruction: Dissolve 900 mL of KHCO₃ in 900 mL de‑ionised water and 100 mL of K₂CO₃ in 100 mL de‑ionised water. Heat gently (≤ 40 °C) to accelerate dissolution, especially of KHCO₃. The final mixing ratio for 3 M KHCO₃ : 3 M K₂CO₃ is 9 : 1. The solution does not require sterilisation; keep the container tightly closed while stirring and heating.

steps.title: Assemble vessel kit and fill reservoir
steps.instruction: Fill the reservoir of the CellDeg system with 200 mL of the bicarbonate‑carbonate buffer prepared in step 3 (this corresponds to 20 % of the total reservoir volume). Attach the CellDeg vessels (prepared in step 2) to the tray positioned on top of the filled reservoir.

steps.title: Cultivate cyanobacteria in CellDeg
steps.instruction: Place the assembled CellDeg system on an orbital shaker (IKA KS 130, orbit 4 mm) set to 320 rpm. Insert the system into a Versatile Environmental Test Chamber (Sanyo) set to 30 °C. Apply the following light‑intensity schedule, measured with a Licor LI‑185B quantum meter: 0–24 h: 250 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹; 24–48 h: 490 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹; from 48 h onward: 750 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹. Replace the bicarbonate‑carbonate buffer in the reservoir after 4 days of cultivation.
